title: Animal Farm
author: George Orwell
Comments:
This book is a true genius in seeing and demonstrating the cycle of power. Orwell here had a near perfect excution of plot and thesis. We see the transition almost live it. The allagory works very well. though Historically Orwell was refering to the USSR, the story applies to many diffrent countries and totalitarian regimes. My favorite character: Boxer, plays a huge role in the argument. Altough I condemn him for his lack of doubt, in a way I cannot blame him for that. As we see most of the animals are uneducated and some are unable to be. And that's something snowball was rooting for. However, Boxer's flaw starts when he set the axiom that Napolian is always right. Boxer's tragedy starts to surface slowly as Napolian shifts more and more to the totalirian regim.
Since Boxer resembles the working class this allegory fits perfectly. Especially the ending where once Boxer was unable to provide any longer he was quickly disposed of just like an old rag that's too dirty to be washed. I liked the character of Binjamin as well, in a way I can relate to him: Though I may be projecting what I want to be I like how Benjamin was always able to see the bigger picture no matter what. Since day one when Napolian kicked Snowball, Benjamin knew that this will end similarly to what Jhonson was doing.
Another point worth mentioning is Squealer: This character is underrated. Napolian isn't as smart as he seems. But he knows where to sit and whom to put where; that's his strength. However, Squealer knows how to handle each and everyone with words making him a scary power.
That led to my conclusion that Napolian knew which force to use and when : His dogs worked on smart and weak animals like the pigs who were with snowball before the exile. On the other hand, Dumb and Strong won't lean in as easily to brute force which we see when dogs tried to attack Boxer he was too strong for them and that's where Squealer comes in. if you think about most are weak and dumb (wd), some are Strong and dumb(Sd), few are Smart and weak (wS), rarely There are those who are Strong and Smart (SS).
wd: follow easily
Sd: use Squaler
wS: use Dogs
SS: will be lonely
In fact, the only character that fits the SS category is Benjamin. Benjamin was smart enough to see what's going on and strng enough to act however he knew he was alone in his consiousness and that led him to be slightly depressive as a character.

title: How  Much Land Does a Man Need
author: Leo Tolstoy
Comments:
A story a bout a farmer Bahom who tried to aquire more and more land Thinking that all his problems were due to the lack of land. One day, to aquire mor land he had to finish a challenge where all he had to do was to circle in 1 day All the land he wants and the land shall be his only if he managed to return to the point where he started otherwise he'd lose the money. And so he did. Trying to seize as much land as he could Bahom managed to return to his starting point only to die on the spot from exauhtion. As a result, he was buried right on the spot with 6-feet of all he needed.
The Story is quite ironic if think about it. As it starts with a comparission between the man of the city and the man of the fields. Ironically, the life of the city was critizied for it's overwhelming anxiety and how the man there is always anxious to do more work to get more money only for Boham- who represents the men of the field - to die from the same anxiety.
